svg.aria-label: AWS credential model after the change: deploys federate from GitHub straight into the customer's role on a subject naming the tenant's environment, and the platform's own account is trusted only for onboarding, bound to the tenant by sts:ExternalId.

g.text: AWS — credential model AFTER (per-tenant federation, onboarding ExternalId)
Still no stored credential. Deploys federate from GitHub straight into the customer's role; the platform's own account is trusted only for onboarding, and only for one tenant.
CONTROL PLANE (platform)
GITHUB ACTIONS RUN
CUSTOMER AWS ACCOUNT
1 · ONBOARDING (ONCE PER TENANT)
sts:AssumeRole — 15 min, ExternalId = tenant ID — writes the secrets
Wizard issues the tenant ID first
A random UUID, generated when the page
opens — before the tenant row exists.
The wizard builds a CloudFormation Quick
Create link with that value in it, to be
applied before the form is submitted.
The operator cannot choose the value.
Not involved
Onboarding is the one step GitHub cannot
do: it runs before any workflow exists.
IAM role, from the customer's bootstrap stack
chatbot-client-deploy-<slug>, two trust statements:
PlatformOnboarding: platform AWS account,
Condition: sts:ExternalId = tenant ID
GitHubActionsDeploy: GitHub's OIDC provider,
sub = repo:…:environment:tenant-<tenant ID>
Both applied before onboarding.
2 · EVERY DEPLOYMENT AND TEARDOWN
Dispatch the workflow
GITHUB_PAT, long-lived
Inputs carry identifiers and ARNs only, plus
tenant_id, which names the GitHub
environment the job runs in.
No secret travels: the LLM, Pinecone and
signer secrets were written into the
customer's Secrets Manager at onboarding.
One hop, short-lived
environment: tenant-<tenant ID>
GitHub signs an OIDC token whose sub
claim carries that environment, and the
run exchanges it with AssumeRoleWith-
WebIdentity on the customer's role (1 h).
The platform's AWS account is not
involved at all.
STS decides, then terraform apply
Subject matches the deploy statement → a
session for this tenant only.
Any other subject → AccessDenied, with
nothing created.
Secrets are resolved at runtime by ARN,
inside the customer's own account.
3 · WHAT THE PLATFORM HOLDS
No AWS credential, and each trust statement names one tenant
Stored: LLM key, Pinecone key and docs-signer secret (AES-256-GCM), erased when the tenant is torn down; PLATFORM_ENCRYPTION_KEY and GITHUB_PAT in the environment.
The ExternalId and the subject are both derived from the tenant's ID. Neither is a secret: both appear in the customer's policy and in CloudTrail.
Closed: a tenant created against another customer's role sends a different ExternalId at onboarding and a different subject on every deploy (see fig-20).
4 · REVOCATION AND BLAST RADIUS
Revocation
The customer deletes the bootstrap stack or edits the
role, and it takes effect immediately.
CloudTrail records AssumeRole with the ExternalId at
onboarding, and AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity with the
token's subject on every deploy and teardown.
What the conditions do not cover
They separate tenants from each other. Anyone who
can change or run the deploy workflows can still name
any tenant's environment, so the repository remains
the trust anchor (Known Limitation #8).
Tenants bootstrapped before this must re-run it.
The same tenant ID names the GitHub environment in the Azure model (fig-23): one identifier, one trust decision per tenant, on both clouds.
